summary: The note surveys emerging sound artists who combine cultural heritage with technology to create immersive auditory experiences. It profiles artists working in AI, social commentary, live 3D sound, collaborative software, synesthesia, community identity and sustainability, with dated performances and releases from September 2023 to June 2024. It concludes that their work offers narratives and encounters that expand how we listen.
one_line: Overview of emerging sound artists blending cultural heritage, AI, immersive performance and sustainability to expand contemporary auditory art in 2023-2024.
key_facts: Mariko Nguyen, a classically trained violinist, performed at the Flux Gallery in September 2023, mixing digitized sounds with her strings and drawing on Japanese, Vietnamese and Scandinavian ambient influences.
Djimon Kassaye, from Addis Ababa, released his debut album "Echoes of Addis" on October 15, 2023, joining traditional Ethiopian scales with urban electronica.
Mirella Costa launched "Voices of the Vanishing" on November 4, 2023, a soundscape project featuring stories and sounds from endangered communities around the world.
Felix Janssens, a Dutch DJ and producer, used AI algorithms in an installation at the Sonic Innovations Expo 2024 in January that changed its output based on visitors' movements and reactions.
Zola Diaz from Mexico City blends traditional Mariachi with Japanese city pop and French electro; her album premiered February 20, 2024 at the Resonance Arts Festival.
Clara Munroe performed a live set on March 3, 2024 at the Paradigm Arts Space using 3D sound modeling and acoustic instruments including a hang drum.
Amir Patel, a music tech graduate of the Berlin University of the Arts, developed software for collaborative sound designing for remote musical partnerships.
As of April 1, 2024, over two hundred collaboration projects had been started globally using Amir Patel's platform.
Lina Kim creates soundscapes mixing everyday urban sounds with traditional Korean instrumentation, fostering communal identity and belonging.
Daniel Forsythe's project "ChromaCoustic", which debuted on May 15, 2024, explores synesthesia by making colors and textures part of the auditory experience.
Sophia Marquez began "Reverb Nature" in June 2024, using recycled materials to build instruments and capturing sounds in nature to compose symphonies.
